mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of at least 0.4 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% indicates a supply-side shock without concurrent labor slack, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for four consecutive months in a late-cycle economy signals accommodative monetary policy that boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 4 consecutive months AND GDP growth < 1.5% for previous 2 quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) of at least 0.5% for three consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in supply capacity, which raises input costs and reduces demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for six consecutive months in a high-capacity utilization environment signals labor market tightness, which elevates wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 growth > 2% for previous 4 quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
